2026 Paris Motor Show • The Volkswagen Group's Affordable BEV Quartet Has Almost Reached 150,000 Orders
The Cuorerosso Shooting Brake Is THE Alfa Romeo We Need – Rendering
15 photos
Photo: Instagram | sugardesign_1
Alfa Romeo has never built an ugly car, and this come from someone who is not necessarily in Alfisti. And not only that, but the Italian auto marque , which operates under Stellantis’ roof, recently unveiled a concept car that stimulates the visual senses.
Presented at the 2026 Paris Motor Show at the beginning of the week, it is called the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso, and it is a concept. However, between us, this thing is much more than a study, because it actually offers a glimpse into the company’s new Bellezza Necessaria design language. And if this is what some future Alfas will look like, then we are glad, because the show car is on the extremely cool side of things from a visual perspective.
Alfa Romeo’s Cuorerosso is a four-door 2+2 that manages to combine elements of traditional Grand Turismos (GTs) and supercars. This means a low-slung profile, and a very long nose, complete with a front fascia that screams Alfa Romeo through its pores. The study features familiar headlights that have a triangular shape and integrated daytime running lights on the upper sections, and a very common-looking grille shape decorated with the corporate logo in the middle, and joined by the Alfa emblem at the tom.
Photo: Instagram | sugardesign_1 The vehicle features a V-shaped front fascia , and it also has a very clean-looking bumper, as well as a fat apron attached to it. As mentioned above, the hood is long, and it sports a pair of creases on it. The profile is on the clean-looking side of things, with its hidden door handles, and tiny mirrors that look like cameras. Further back, we can see a very large ducktail spoiler, a pair of round taillights, the Alfa Rome lettering, a Scudetto-shaped rear window, and stacked exhaust tips in the middle of the bumper.
Now, as we already told you, the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso Concept is a 2+2 sedan, but it was only natural that someone out there would eventually turn it into something else. That someone is known as @sugardesign_1 on Instagram, and that something is a station wagon. This CGI-infused car has a longer roofline than the real thing, redesigned rear windows, rear three-quarter windows, different rear three-quarter panels, thicker rear pillars, a tailgate that opens up into a larger cargo area, and a rear windscreen that is significantly less racked.
Everything else carries over from the actual car , including the front fascia, the red paint finish, the typical Alfa Romeo wheels in gold, and so on. The same goes for the cockpit, which is on the stylish side of things, especially when comparing it to the company’s rivals. The interior is said to have been inspired by the 1967 33 Stradale, and features a simple dashboard panel, a pair of round gauges that can blend into a single one behind the yoke-like steering wheel, and a floating-style central spine, physical controls, circular air vents, and so on.
It this thing were real, then it would also sport red and black leather, and would send the same Italian vibe. And that’s definitely not all, because the same powertrain would be found under the hood. And in case you haven’t heard, the new Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso Concept is equipped with the same engine as the Quadrifoglio versions of the Giulia and Stelvio. This means a V6 mill with twin turbocharging and a 2.9-liter displacement.
Photo: Instagram | sugardesign_1 The lump pumps out 505 horsepower and 442 pound-feet (600 Nm) of torque, or 533 hp in the GTA and GTAm, and in this case, it is assisted by a hybrid system. A torque converter transmission, a driveshaft made of carbon fiber, and all-wheel drive are on deck. However, the Italian company hasn’t released the performance numbers, and also hasn’t spoken about the total output and thrust of its Cuorerosso show car, but this model is definitely something to write home about, and this applies not only to the powertrain, but also the exterior design, and the cockpit.
But will it reach production? Chances are that it won’t, but some of its styling cues could eventually be adopted by future Alfa Romeo models. Deep down, we wish the Cuorerosso got approved for production, because such a thing would obviously pose a major threat to other sports sedans, including the electrified four-pot Mercedes-AMG C 63, the new Audi RS 5 Sedan, and the upcoming BMW M3, which is in the making, and will adopt the Neue Klasse design language.
If it were really going after the likes of the above-mentioned models, then the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso would clearly be joined by the wagon version rendered here, as this thing looks like the perfect alternative to the Audi RS 5 Avant, and a BMW M3 Touring killer at this point. Truth be told, I love both the sedan and the rendered estate, and the latter has got to be one of the best looking CGI projects we have encountered all week.
